question: A 67-year-old man with dilated cardiomyopathy is admitted to the cardiac care unit (CCU) because of congestive heart failure exacerbation. A medical student wants to determine the flow velocity across the aortic valve. She estimates the cross-sectional area of the valve is 5 cm2and the volumetric flow rate is 55 cm3/s. Which of the following best represents this patient's flow velocity across the aortic valve?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Cross-sectional area of aortic valve is 5 cm²" -> "Volumetric flow rate is 55 cm³/s" -> "Flow velocity can be calculated using the formula: velocity = flow rate / area" -> "Flow velocity = 55 cm³/s / 5 cm²" -> "Flow velocity = 11 cm/s" -> "Convert to m/s: 11 cm/s = 0.11 m/s" -> 95%

enhanced_information: To determine the flow velocity across the aortic valve, we use the formula: velocity = flow rate / area. Given a cross-sectional area of 5 cm² and a volumetric flow rate of 55 cm³/s, the calculation is as follows: Flow velocity = 55 cm³/s / 5 cm² = 11 cm/s. Converting this to meters per second gives 11 cm/s = 0.11 m/s. This calculation is consistent with standard medical principles regarding flow dynamics. Therefore, the best representation of the patient's flow velocity across the aortic valve is 0.11 m/s.
